- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 30-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.5) and price is falling, model underestimates; adjust downward by 1–3% per sentiment unit above 0.5.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use 14-day smoothed sentiment as trigger.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior, 30% current) to dampen noise.
